Package com.nexuslink.protocol.rabbitmq

Class RabbitMqService

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.rabbitmq.RabbitMqService
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class RabbitMqService extends Object implements AutoCloseable
RabbitMQ client wrapper over the official Java amqp-client (AMQP 0.9.1). Connect to a broker (via an amqp:///amqps:// URI or a bare host[:port]), declare exchanges/queues and bindings, publish messages to an exchange + routing key, and stream deliveries from a queue to a listener.

A single Connection and Channel are kept in memory; all I/O is blocking, so the UI drives it on a background Task, mirroring the other protocol services. The factoryFor(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String) helper is pure (no network I/O) and is the unit-tested seam.

    • factoryFor

      public static com.rabbitmq.client.ConnectionFactory factoryFor(String target, String username, String password) throws Exception
      Builds and configures a ConnectionFactory from a connection string — pure, performs no network I/O, so it is fully unit-testable. target may be a full amqp:// / amqps:// URI (credentials in the URI win) or a bare host / host:port; username/password are applied when non-blank and not already set by a URI.

This is the message-properties-editor path; the pure buildProperties(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>) builder is the tested seam.

    • publishConfirmed

      public PublishConfirm publishConfirmed(String exchange, String routingKey, String body, long timeoutMs) throws IOException, InterruptedException
      Publishes body like publish(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String), then waits for a publisher confirm from the broker and reports whether it was PublishConfirm.ACKED, PublishConfirm.NACKED or PublishConfirm.TIMEOUT. confirmSelect() is enabled once per channel (lazily, on first use). A timeoutMs of 0 waits indefinitely.

      Requires a live broker for an end-to-end run (the wire round-trip and confirm); the pure boolean-to-outcome mapping it relies on is unit-tested via PublishConfirm.

      Throws:
      IOException
      InterruptedException

    • consume

      public String consume(String queue, boolean autoAck) throws IOException
      Starts consuming from queue, routing each delivery to the registered listener. Returns the consumer tag (pass to cancel(java.lang.String)). With autoAck false, deliveries are acknowledged automatically once handed to the listener.
      Throws:
      IOException

    • consumeManual

      public String consumeManual(String queue) throws IOException
      Starts consuming from queue with auto-ack OFF, handing each delivery (including its RabbitMqService.Incoming.deliveryTag()) to the registered listener without acknowledging it. The caller is then responsible for calling ack(long) or nack(long, boolean) for every delivery tag. Returns the consumer tag (pass to cancel(java.lang.String)).

      Requires a live broker for an end-to-end run.

      Throws:
      IOException

    • ack

      public void ack(long deliveryTag) throws IOException
      Acknowledges a single delivery by tag (the broker may then discard the message). Pair with consumeManual(java.lang.String). Requires a live broker for an end-to-end run.
      Throws:
      IOException

    • nack

      public void nack(long deliveryTag, boolean requeue) throws IOException
      Negatively acknowledges a single delivery by tag. When requeue is true the broker re-queues the message for redelivery, otherwise it is dropped (or dead-lettered if configured). Pair with consumeManual(java.lang.String). Requires a live broker for an end-to-end run.
      Throws:
      IOException
